thread:
Ava (Support): Hey folks, paging SRE/runtime — Customer ACME reported p99 generation latency jumping from ~1.2s to ~8–12s across several regions starting ~08:20 UTC. They see lots of 202/queued responses in app logs. Can we triage?

Ravi (SRE): I’m looking. Grafana shows a spike in request queue length and admission drops for model-retro/v3 around 08:17 UTC. p95 up from 300ms -> 2.1s, p99 up to ~11s. CPU on async-workers nodes is fine but there are many tasks stuck in the local async queue. Could be backlog at worker-side (threadpool saturation) or KV cache hot-miss storm.

Maya (Runtime): Noted. Any deploys around that time?

DeployBot: deploy redwood/runtime:v2026.03.15-rc4 completed on cluster-us-west-2 at 08:10 UTC by Jon.

Jon (Eng-Platform): I rolled the rc to a small subset for canary at 08:10, then widened at 08:15. Canary logs showed increased tail latency but we didn't flag it. I'll rollback if you want.

Ravi (SRE): Hold on rollback for now — we need quick mitigations. Hypothesis: the new runtime path shrank the async executor pool size under certain memory conditions; combined with higher input lengths from ACME leads to queueing. Looking at /metrics: `admit_queue_length{model="retro/v3"}` jumped from ~20 -> 620. Admission controller started rejecting and routing to lower tiers.

Maya (Runtime): I can patch the executor config to increase `executor.max_workers` and reduce `batch_window_ms` for that model. That should drop queueing. Will push a hot-config to active config store.

Ava (Support): Customer asked for a temporary workaround: can we divert their traffic to a smaller model variant until we stabilize?

Ravi (SRE): Yes, we can add a routing override for ACME’s API key to route to `retro/v3-compact` which has lower memory usage and slightly different perf profile. Doing that now.

Jon (Eng-Platform): Before we change routing, attaching a quick check command for anyone oncall: `curl -sS https://metrics.redwood.internal/api/query?expr=admit_queue_length%7Bmodel%3D%22retro%2Fv3%22%7D
` — shows the current backlog. Also `redis-cli -h queue-cache info` shows increased `blocked_clients`.

Maya (Runtime): Pushing config change: updating `executor.max_workers=48` -> `96` for model `retro/v3` in active config. Also reducing `batch_window_ms` from `20` -> `10` for lower latency (trade: small perf loss). Rolling to 3% of nodes now for safety.

Ravi (SRE): I’m temporarily increasing the admission concurrency for the model: `admit.max_inflight=120` -> `240` at the router tier so more requests are admitted while we verify worker scaling. Also enabling fallback routing to `retro/v3-compact` on overload after 500ms queueing.

Ava (Support): I told ACME support contact we’re routing them to compact model and applying fixes; they asked for repro steps in case they want to simulate.

Maya (Runtime): Repro steps I used locally: run a steady request generator hitting `retro/v3` with input lengths ~2048 tokens and concurrency 200. Sample load command:```bash
wrk -t10 -c200 -d120s --script=gen.lua http://runtime-service.local/v1/generate
```Logs you’ll want: runtime worker stack traces + local threadpool metrics: `GET /debug/executor`

Ravi (SRE): Observed worker thread dumps show lots of tasks waiting on KV cache fetches (cache-miss storm). Metric `kv_cache.misses_per_sec` spiked x8. Might be correlated to recent cache eviction policy change in rc4.

Jon (Eng-Platform): I can revert the cache eviction change quickly. The change was `cache.eviction_policy=adaptive` -> previous `lru_static`. Rolling that back to canary nodes now.

DeployBot: config-rollout cache.eviction_policy revert to lru_static initiated by Jon at 08:44 UTC.

Maya (Runtime): Hot-config applied to executor and admission on canaries — I see admit_queue_length on canaries dropping ~60% after config change. Non-canary nodes still catching up.

Ravi (SRE): For immediate customer relief: 1) ACME traffic routed to `retro/v3-compact` (done) 2) admission concurrency increased 3) executor pool bumped on canaries 4) cache eviction reverted. I'll keep watch and let Support know when p99 falls below 2s.

Ava (Support): ACME confirmed latency improved to ~1.4s p99 after reroute. They still see occasional 5–6s spikes, asked for ETA on full fix.

Maya (Runtime): ETA for full rollout of executor patch + cache revert: ~25–35 minutes if no regressions. After that we should run a targeted load test to validate tail latency. I'll schedule the load test and post results.

Ravi (SRE): Action items: - Monitor `admit_queue_length`, `kv_cache.misses_per_sec`, `executor.waiters`, `router.admit_rejections` - If p99 remains >3s after full rollout, rollback runtime:v2026.03.15-rc4 and re-open canary. - Prepare postmortem for change to cache eviction + executor defaults.

Jon (Eng-Platform): Adding a temporary alert rule to paging: `admit_queue_length > 200 for 2m` to trigger sooner.

Ava (Support): Thank you all — I’ll keep ACME updated and escalate to CSM if needed. Marking thread resolved for now, will reopen if latency recurs. :white_check_mark:

Maya (Runtime): Posting follow-up load test results in ~30m.

Ravi (SRE): Monitoring. If anyone needs quick commands for debugging, paste `curl` hits to /debug/executor and small sampling of `strace` of stuck workers.

(End of thread)
